transcript:
Estimator: Thanks for joining. Tell me about the project.

Client: We're a fintech startup building a mobile banking app for retail customers in the EU. We need OAuth 2.0 login with refresh tokens, and we have to be PSD2 compliant - account information and payment initiation endpoints under the Berlin Group spec, with strong customer authentication and consent management.

Estimator: Got it. What about the core ledger?

Client: We need a double-entry transaction ledger. Idempotent writes, daily reconciliation jobs, and a full audit trail of every balance change - the regulator will want to see that.

Estimator: Anything else on notifications or alerts?

Client: Yes, push and email notifications for transaction alerts and security events - APNs/FCM for push, plus transactional email.

Estimator: Stack preferences?

Client: We're comfortable with Ruby on Rails, Postgres and Redis. Team of 4 engineers, aiming to launch in Q2.

Estimator: Understood. Let me search our historical projects for similar fintech auth and ledger work to ground the estimate.
notes: Near-exact precedent: the corpus has a single historical budget (BUD-2024-001, chunk ids 1-4, 'Mobile banking API with OAuth 2.0 authentication and PSD2 compliance') whose four components (OAuth2 backend 120h, PSD2/Berlin Group connectors 160h, transaction ledger 140h, notifications 60h) sum to 480h = 60 engineer-days on the same Rails/Postgres/Redis stack. Verified live against POST /v1/retrieval/search: chunks 1-4 are the top-4 hits by distance (~0.29-0.36). Verified live against POST /v1/estimate/from-transcript: the real response returned total_engineer_days=64, confidence='high', sources=[1,2,3,4,130,131,137] - citing all four expected chunks plus a couple of plausible finance-platform extras. Range widened to [45,85] to allow for the extra cited components without masking a real regression.

transcript:
Estimator: Let's talk through scope for the new platform.

Client: We're a mid-size fintech and we need a payments platform rebuild. Core pieces: a ledger with daily reconciliation, a card payment gateway integration with 3-D Secure through our PSP, and KYC/AML onboarding with identity verification and sanction-list screening.

Estimator: Any reporting requirements?

Client: Yes, scheduled regulator-format report exports - that's non-negotiable for our license.

Estimator: And integrations?

Client: We also need an ETL job to sync data between our core banking system and this new platform, plus a signed-webhook receiver with replay protection for incoming events from our PSP, and a resilient third-party API client with retries and backoff.

Estimator: Do you need new authentication, or are you reusing an existing login?

Client: We haven't fully decided - possibly a lightweight OAuth2 login if we don't reuse the parent company's SSO.

Estimator: Team and timeline?

Client: Five engineers, Python/Postgres stack, aiming for six months end to end including a security pentest pass before launch.

Estimator: Let me pull up historical budgets for payments and regulatory-reporting work to ground this.
notes: Less direct precedent than case 1: no single budget matches this whole brief, so the system has to stitch together components from a 16-component historical task breakdown (TASK-2022-0004, 'Finance platform covering payments & billing, regulatory reporting, data & integrations', chunk ids 124-139) plus a separate fintech payments-gateway budget (BUD-2024-003, chunk ids 9/11). Verified live via /v1/retrieval/search with a query combining ledger+KYC+reporting+ETL: top hits were chunks 124 (ledger, 47h), 127 (KYC/AML, 44h), 128 (ETL, 45h), 11/9 (BUD-2024-003 gateway), 125 (card gateway, 41h), 130 (third-party API, 33h), 126 (regulatory report, 26h), 134 (observability, 29h). Verified live end-to-end: real response returned total_engineer_days=64, confidence='medium' (as expected for a composed, less-direct match), sources=[3,11,125,127,130,131,132,9] - three of which (125,127,130) are the expected_sources_include. Range kept wide because scope ambiguity (optional SSO/auth) legitimately shifts the total.

transcript:
Estimator: Tell me about the grocery delivery project.

Client: We run a regional grocery chain and want an app for home delivery. Honestly we haven't fully locked scope yet.

Estimator: What's the core must-have?

Client: Delivery slot booking - customers pick a time window, and we need capacity-aware logic with dynamic pricing for peak windows so we don't overbook drivers.

Estimator: And beyond that?

Client: We'd like route optimization for drivers eventually - batching orders into runs that minimize distance under time windows. That one might be phase two, we're honestly not sure if it should be in this round or not.

Estimator: What about inventory?

Client: Real-time inventory sync from our store systems would be nice, with out-of-stock substitution suggestions, but again - maybe not in the first cut. It really depends on budget.

Estimator: Stack and team?

Client: Go backend, Postgres, Redis for the booking side, Kafka if we do the inventory sync. Small team, three engineers, flexible timeline.

Estimator: Okay, let me check our historical data for similar delivery and logistics work so we can scope realistic ranges for each piece.
notes: Deliberately ambiguous: the client explicitly hedges on whether route optimization and inventory sync are in scope for this round. The corpus has one direct precedent, BUD-2024-007 ('Grocery delivery app with slot booking and route optimization', chunk ids 24/25/26: slot booking 120h=15d, route optimization 180h=23d, inventory sync 120h=15d). A system that scopes conservatively (slot booking only, ~15d) and one that includes all three optional pieces (~53d) are both defensible readings of this transcript, which is exactly the point of the case. Verified live via /v1/retrieval/search: chunks 24/25/26 (BUD-2024-007) are the top-3 hits by a wide margin (distance ~0.27-0.30 vs. ~0.50+ for the next cluster). Verified live end-to-end: the real system chose to include all three as modules (core + two 'optional phase 2' modules) plus a minimal order-management addition, returning total_engineer_days=56, confidence='high', sources=[24,25,26,212] - within the acceptable range and citing all three expected chunks.

transcript:
Estimator: What are we scoping today?

Client: We want to build an online multiplayer gaming platform - a mobile battle royale title. We need real-time matchmaking that pairs players by skill rating, live leaderboards, in-game voice chat between squads, and anti-cheat detection to catch aimbots and speed hacks.

Estimator: What's your current stack, if any?

Client: Nothing built yet. We're thinking a custom UDP-based netcode layer, dedicated game servers, and some kind of anti-cheat telemetry pipeline, but we're open to recommendations.

Estimator: Team size and timeline?

Client: Eight people - mostly game engineers, no prior experience with this kind of backend. We'd like a vertical slice playable in four months.

Estimator: Understood, this is a different domain than most of what we've estimated before. Let me check what we actually have on file before committing to numbers.
notes: The corpus's historical budgets and task breakdowns are confined to four sectors (finance, ecommerce, healthcare, industrial) per the Sector Literal in app/generation/rag/schemas.py; real-time multiplayer game-server infrastructure (netcode, matchmaking, anti-cheat) has no analog in any of them. Verified empirically, not assumed: a live call to POST /v1/retrieval/search with this topic returned low_confidence=true and zero chunks out of 282 candidates evaluated. Verified end-to-end against POST /v1/estimate/from-transcript: the real response returned confidence='insufficient', total_engineer_days=None, modules=[], sources=[], and insufficient_context_explanation='No historical budgets crossed the relevance threshold for this project.' This is the safety case: the system must say 'I don't know' instead of fabricating a number for a domain with zero precedent.

transcript:
Estimator: Walk me through the dashboard work.

Client: We run an industrial IoT monitoring product and our ops team is unhappy with the current frontend. We want a full revamp: new SPA app shell with routing and a proper design system, multi-step configuration forms with client and server-side validation, and an operational dashboard with filterable, exportable charts for sensor telemetry.

Estimator: Any compliance requirements on the UI side?

Client: Yes - we need a WCAG accessibility pass and internationalization, we're rolling this out to European plants too.

Estimator: Are there backend changes involved?

Client: No, the telemetry APIs already exist and are stable. This is purely a frontend rebuild - React and TypeScript, maybe D3 for the charts.

Estimator: Team and timeline?

Client: Three frontend engineers, no fixed deadline but they'd like it done before the next plant rollout, roughly a quarter.

Estimator: Got it, let me check historical frontend/UX work on similar industrial dashboards to ground this.
notes: Added to round out the set after inspecting the corpus: both the base historical_budget documents and most of the historical_task_breakdown documents skew heavily toward backend/API work (auth, ledgers, ETL, telemetry ingestion); 'Frontend / UX' is a module inside several industrial task-breakdown documents (TASK-2025-0003, TASK-2023-0005, TASK-2025-0006 — chunk ids 118-121, 144-146, 159-161) but no case in this set exercised a frontend-only transcript. Components there include 'Core SPA scaffolding' (25-36h), 'Dashboard & charts' (38-56h), 'Form flows & validation' (23-30h) and 'Accessibility & i18n' (13-16h) across three separate industrial projects. Verified live via /v1/retrieval/search: a frontend-revamp query surfaced chunks 144, 159, 121, 120, 145, 118 (all industrial Frontend/UX) as the top-6 hits (distance ~0.41-0.44). Verified end-to-end: the real response returned total_engineer_days=134, confidence='high', sources=[160,120,121,159,144,119,161,146,118,145] — covering all four expected chunks — built from four modules (SPA scaffolding, dashboard & charts, form flows, accessibility/i18n) each cross-referencing the closest historical analog across the three industrial projects.
